reader.requirement: At --std 85 TERMINATE naming several reports behaves as separate TERMINATE statements in written order: each report's control footings, page footing and report footing (with its own prior-value bracket) complete before the next report starts, a report with no GENERATE produces nothing, and an unsuccessful one does not stop the rest.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Has(2002): the contained-program GLOBAL-file requirement is not asked at 85
DialectBehavior.TerminateDiscardsSavedNextGroup: at 85 the saved absolute NEXT GROUP is kept for the first control footing
DialectBehavior.ControlFootingPageGroupsSeePriorControlValues: which control values PF/PH see during TERMINATE's footing phase

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the per-report split (BoundImplicitSeries of one BoundTerminate per name, one engine Terminate call each) is edition-free; the edition arms above change what one report's TERMINATE does, not the multi-name composition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c33 covers written order and file left open; per-report completion of the control-footing bracket, a report with no GENERATE in the list, a repeated name and a contained-program TERMINATE are not exercised

probes.printed: TERMINATE R-B R-C R-A: CF-B K=2 J=5 / RF-B K=2 J=5 / CF-A K=1 J=6 / RF-A K=1 J=6 / AFTER K=2 J=6; R-C file empty
probes.expected: R-B completely (prior J, J restored), R-C nothing (GR2), then R-A completely

probes.printed: TERMINATE R-A R-A R-B: RF-A 1, RF-B 2 (second R-A inactive, skipped, R-B still terminated); separate TERMINATE R-A. TERMINATE R-B. behaves the same: RF-B 3
contained program TERMINATE R-B R-A of GLOBAL reports with non-GLOBAL FDs: compiles, both RFs printed
probes.expected: accepted at 85 (no 1985 GLOBAL-file rule), each terminated

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.4.7.4 GR5  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: The binder builds one BoundTerminate per report-name inside a BoundImplicitSeries, so each report is a separate implicit statement with its own resumption point; the emitter writes one engine Terminate per report in written order.

refuter.evidence: Probe t1_shared_file.cob (--std 85): two reports in ONE file (REPORTS ARE R-A R-B), different control priors (R-A last generated with K=1, R-B with K=2, K=3 at TERMINATE), a USE on RF-B that changes WS-T SOURCEd by R-A's groups; TERMINATE R-B R-A wrote CFB 2 00 / RFB 2 10, then CFA 1 11 / PFA 11 / RFA 1 11, and K=3 after: R-B completed (its own prior bracket and restore) before R-A began, R-A's groups saw R-B's USE side effect, exactly as two separate statements in written order. First attempt refused PF SOURCE of the control item (COBOL6825, §1985:XIII.3.20.3 SR5, correct and unrelated). u1_dummy_use.cob: a TERMINATE after INITIATE with no GENERATE runs no USE and produces nothing (GR2). cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.4.7.4 GR5.
